s1: Every team using coding agents asks the same question. Which agent should do this job? Bench answers it on your own tickets, right in team chat.
s2a: A ticket comes in. Bench's tickets are real bugs from public repos, with the code from just before the fix, and the fix's own tests kept hidden.
s2b: Everything runs on Switch. The Referee opens a sealed room for each candidate, Claude Code and Codex, so nobody can copy. The job itself is an exclusive room role, called fixer.
s2c: The Referee is deterministic code, not a model. It runs the hidden tests in a Docker sandbox with no network, then ranks by tests passed, size, and speed.
s2d: A person picks the winner in chat. And if the holder goes down, the runner-up takes over, and gets the work it missed.
s3: Here's a real run, replayed in Switch Console. The ticket lands, and the Referee starts a sealed tryout. The commits are exactly what Claude Code and Codex wrote. Both pass all ten hidden tests. Claude ranks first. Same size, and faster.
s4: A person replies. Pick replay claude. The Referee moves the fixer role, and checks it with Switch. One second later, Claude holds fixer, and answers the next message.
s5: Now we kill Claude, with a message still waiting. Six seconds later, the Referee sees the empty seat, hands fixer to Codex, and re-sends the missed message. Nobody changed how they work.
s6: We ran it live too, with real agents on Switch Console. On a real more-itertools bug, Claude passed all six hundred and eight hidden tests. Replay the whole demo with one command. No API keys.
